### CHAP. I.

*1. The World of Life or Forms, and the potentiality of the visible universe created by the Triune God, and referred to a Monad or Unity. 6. The universal, immense matter of the visible world created out of nothing, and referred to the number Two. 7. Why it was not said of this matter that it was "good." 9. The ordering of an Earth or planet to make it conveniently habitable, referred to the number Three. 14. The immense ethereal matter, or Heaven, organized into suns or planets, both primary and secondary (namely, both Earths and Moons), and referred to the number Four. 20. The replenishing of an Earth with fish and fowl, referred to the number Five. 24. The creation of beasts and cattle, but most especially of humanity itself, referred to the number Six.*

<margin>1.</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter O, featuring stylized floral patterns and foliage within a double-lined square border.</image-desc>Our design being to set out the more conspicuous parts of the external Creation before we descend to the genealogies and successions of mankind, there are two notable objects that present themselves to our understanding, which we must first take notice of, as having a universal influence upon all that follows. These I symbolically decipher, the one by the name of *Heaven and Light* (for I mean the same thing by both these terms), and the other by the name of *Earth*. By *Heaven* or *Light*, you are to understand *the complete collection of intellectual spirits*, the souls of men and beasts, and the seminal forms <note>original: "Seminal forms"; these are the underlying spiritual blueprints or life-principles that govern the growth and form of all physical things</note> of all things, which you may call, if you please, *The World of Life*. By *Earth*, you are to understand the *potentiality* or *capability* for the existence of the outward Creation. This possibility is presented to our minds as the result of the omnipotence of God, without whom nothing would exist; it is indeed the furthest shadow and darkest projection of that power, which also involves the incompatibility <note>original: "Incompoſſibility"; the state of things that cannot coexist or are logically inconsistent</note> and incommensurability <note>original: "Incommenſurability"; the quality of things having no common measure or being vastly different in nature</note> of things. The *Triune God*, therefore, by His eternal wisdom, first created this symbolic *Heaven* and *Earth*.

Therefore the entire Deity, by an inward *Word* (which is nothing but *wisdom and power* sharpened with *actual will*), with more ease than we can present any concept or idea to our own minds, actually exhibited to their own view the whole creation of spiritual substances. 4. And God approved of and was pleased with all this as good. But even though in his plan there was a settlement of the *fluid darkness* or *obscure possibility* of the outward creation, it still remained only a *dark possibility*. Indeed, there was a notorious <note>In this context, "notorious" means well-known or clearly evident, rather than having a negative connotation.</note> distinction between this *actual spiritual creation* and the *dim possibility* of the material or outward world.

5. To such an extent that the one might very well be called *Day* and the other *Night*. This is because *Night* erases and blots out all the distinct shapes and colors of things, but *Day* shows them all orderly and clearly to our sight. Thus, the *immaterial creature* <note>meaning: the spiritual world or spiritual beings</note> was perfectly finished, being an inexhaustible treasure of light and form for decorating and completing the material world, and for providing a *Morning* or *active principle* to every *passive one* in the future parts of the physical creation. But in this *first day's work*, as we will call it, the *morning* and *evening* are purely *metaphysical*. For the *active* and *passive* principles here are not two distinct *substances* (one *material* and the other *spiritual*); rather, the *passive principle* is *matter* that is merely *metaphysical*, and indeed is no real or actual entity. As has been already said, it is quite divided from the *light* or *spiritual substance*, not belonging to it but to the outward world, of which it is the shadowy possibility. But however they may be, this *passive* and *active* principle are the *first day’s work*: a *monad* <term>original: "Monad"; a single, indivisible unit, used here to symbolize spiritual unity</term> or *unity* being such a fitting symbol of the *immaterial nature*.

This is a *substance* which you must imagine to lie between the previously mentioned *fluid possibility of natural things* and the *region of seminal forms*—not that these things are separated by physical location, but according to a more intellectual order.

8. Therefore, *this matter* was immediately set in motion and stirred at its very creation by the hand that made it. Just as a primary planet is rightly called a *planet* because it reflects light, it is also rightly called an *Earth* because of its habitability. God organizes these Earths so that they neither lack water to rest upon them, nor are they entirely covered by water—even though they are surrounded by the fluid air (which contains that *ether* or *heaven*). Under this air, the waters would have flooded the face of the Earth if His providence had not gathered them into one place.

10. Thus, He created both dry land and the seas, rivers, and springs for the benefits that are obvious to everyone.

11. He also decorates the ground with grass, herbs, and flowers, and has wisely provided seeds so that they may reproduce, ensuring the continuation of such useful things on the face of the earth.

The fifth day’s work; and the *Five-fold* <note>original: "Quinary"</note> number denotes the nature of it.

24. 25. And when he had made them in this way, he approved of them as good.

26. Then God, reflecting upon his own nature and viewing himself—consulting with his own *Beyond-essential Goodness* <note>original: "Super-essential Goodness," a Neoplatonic term for the highest aspect of the Divine</note>, the *Eternal Intellect*, and the unquenchable *Love-flame of his Omnipotent Spirit*—concluded to make a far higher kind of living creature than had yet been brought into the world. Thus, Man appeared upon the stage of the Earth as Lord of all living creatures. For it was only right that he who bears the *Image* of the invisible God should be the supreme monarch of this visible world. And what can be more like God than the soul of man, which is so free, so rational, and so intellectual? Furthermore, he is no less like God now that he is united to a terrestrial body; his soul or spirit possesses and penetrates <note>original: "striking through"</note> a condensed <note>original: "compendious"</note> collection of all kinds of physical matter, managing it while his understanding remains free to think of other things—just as God gives life to <note>original: "vivificates"</note> and actuates the whole world while remaining entirely free to contemplate himself. Therefore, God gave Man dominion over the birds of the air, the fish of the sea, and the beasts of the earth; for it is reasonable that the lesser should be in service to the better.

27. Thus God created Man in his own *Image*, consisting of an Intellectual Soul and a Terrestrial Body activated by it. Therefore, mankind became Male and Female, just as other land animals are.

28. And the blessing of Divine Wisdom for the reproduction of their kind was evident in the design of the body parts framed for that purpose. As they grew in number, they ruled over the Earth and mastered the beasts of the field through their power and cleverness <note>original: "policy"</note>; they fed themselves with fish, fowl, and whatever else pleased them and contributed to their satisfaction; for all was given to them by right of their creation.

29. And so that nothing might be missing for their delight, behold, Divine Providence has also prepared for their palate all precious and pleasant herbs for salads, and provided them banquets of the most delicate fruit from the fruit-bearing trees.

30. But as for the coarser grass and inferior kinds of herbs, they are intended for the inferior and lower kinds of creatures. Therefore, Man is free to seek out his own food and make use of it.

31. And God, considering everything he had made, approved of it as very good. The union of the *Passive* and *Active* principle was the *Sixth* day’s work; and the *Six-fold* <note>original: "Senary"</note> number denotes the nature of it.

2. *God's full and absolute Rest from creating anything anew, symbolized <note>original: "adumbrated"</note> by the number Seven. 4. Suns and Planets are not only the ornaments but the effects of the Ethereal Matter or Heaven. 6. The manner of Man and other Animals rising out of the Earth by the power of God in Nature. 8. How it was with Adam before he descended into flesh and became an Earthly Animal. 10. That the four Cardinal Virtues were in Adam in his Ethereal or Paradisiacal condition. 17. That this sense and joy of the Life of the Vehicle is in itself without either blame or shame.*

1. **T**hus the Heavens and the Earth were finished, and all the ornaments <note>original: "garnishings"</note> of them, such as Trees, Flowers, and Herbs; Suns, Moons, and Stars; Fishes, Fowls, and Beasts of the field; and the greatest of all, Man himself.

2. Therefore, God having thus completed his work in the six-fold order <note>original: "Senary," referring to the six days of creation</note>, comprising the whole Creation in *Six* orders of things, he ceased from ever creating anything more, either in this outward *Material* world, or in the world of Life. Instead, his Creative Power retiring into himself, he enjoyed his own eternal *Rest*, which is his unchanging and tireless Nature; with ease, he oversees the whole range of Beings, and continues to provide *Essence, Life*, and *Activity* to them. He better rectifies the worse, and all are guided by his Eternal Word and Spirit; but no new Substance has been ever created since the *Six* days' production of things, nor shall ever be hereafter.

3. For this *Seventh day*, God has made an *Eternal Holy Day*, or *Festival of Rest* for himself, wherein he will only please himself by beholding the exquisite Order, Motion, and right Nature of things. His *Wisdom, Justice*, and *Mercy* unavoidably weave themselves <note>original: "insinuating themselves"</note>, according to the established frame of the World, into all the parts of the Creation, since he has *Ministers of his Goodness and Wrath* prepared everywhere. Thus, he himself needs only to look on and see the effects of that divine retribution <note>original: "Nemesis," the Greek goddess of inescapable destiny or retribution, here used to mean the natural consequences built into the moral order</note> that is necessarily interwoven in the nature of the things themselves which he has made. This, therefore, is that *Sabbath* or *Festival of Rest* which God himself is said to celebrate on the *Seventh day*; and indeed, the number itself declares its nature.

4. And now to open my mind more fully and plainly to you, I must tell you that those things which I previously termed the *Garnishings* of the Heaven and of the Earth are not only ornaments, but the *Generations* of them. I say, *Plants* and *Animals* were the *Generations, Effects*, and *Productions* of the Earth; the *Seminal Forms* <note>The spiritual blueprints or "seeds" that give shape and life to matter</note> and *Souls of Animals* weave themselves <note>original: "insinuating," continued on the next page</note>...

# The Philosophic Cabbala. CHAP. II.

...insinuating themselves into the prepared matter of it; and **Suns**, **Planets**, or **Earths** were the offspring <note>original: "Generations"</note> or products of the **Heavens**. Energy and motion were granted from the **World of Life** to the immense body of the Universe. So, what I previously called mere ornaments <note>original: "Garnishings"</note> are indeed the products or offspring of the Heavens and the Earth as soon as they were made. I do not take it upon myself to define the exact time in which God made the Heavens and the Earth; for He might do it all at once by His absolute omnipotence, or He might—after creating all substance, both material and spiritual—let them act upon one another over such periods of time as the nature of the production of the things themselves required.

5. However, it was for religious <note>original: "pious"</note> purposes that I organized the Creation into that order of **six days**. This was to firmly root in the hearts of the people this grand and useful truth: *That the omnipotence of God is such that He can act above and even contrary to natural causes*. This is why I mentioned the herbs and plants of the field before I noted either rain or a man to perform gardening and husbandry. Indeed, according to my former narrative, there had been no such kind of rain as normally waters the labors of the farmer today.

6. But instead, a moist vapor rose up from the Earth. Being matured and refined <note>original: "concocted"</note> by the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Anima Mundi*, the "soul of the world" that animates physical matter</note>—which is very active in the heavens or the air—it became a precious, balmy liquid and a suitable medium <note>original: "vehicle"</note> of life. This descended like dewy showers upon the face of the Earth and moistened the ground. Thus, the warmth of the Sun gently playing upon the surface prepared matter in various ways for many kinds of things—not only for the seeds <note>original: "Seminal forms"</note> of **plants**, but for the souls of **animals** as well.

7. And **Man** himself rose out of the Earth in this manner: the dust of the ground was rightly prepared and tempered by these rich <note>original: "unctuous"</note> showers and balmy droppings from heaven. For God had so designed by His infinite wisdom that matter prepared in this specific way should, by a natural affinity <note>original: "Vital congruity"</note>, attract corresponding forms from the **World of Life**. That world is everywhere close at hand and densely inhabits <note>original: "inequitate," literally to ride upon or guide as a horseman</note> the moist and rich air. Therefore, in this manner, the **Aerial** or **Ethereal Adam** was conveyed into an earthly body, having his most significant residence in the head or brain. And thus, **Adam** became the soul of a **living creature on Earth**.

8. But I shall declare to you how it was with **Adam** before he descended into this lower condition of life in the symbolic <note>original: "Ænigmatical"</note> narrative that follows: The Lord God had planted a garden eastward in **Eden**, where He had placed the Man whom He afterward formed into a **terrestrial animal**. For **Adam** was first entirely ethereal and placed in Paradise—that is, in a happy and joyful condition of the spirit. He was placed under the strengthening beams of the **Divine Intellect**, and the "Sun of Righteousness" then shone brightly upon him.

9. And his soul was like the ground which God has blessed; it brought forth every pleasant tree and every goodly plant of his heavenly Father’s own planting. For the holy **Spirit of Life** had enriched the soil so that it brought forth all manner of pleasant and profitable fruits.

9. And the **Tree of Life** was in the midst of this Garden of man's soul, namely, the **Essential Will of God**, which is the true root of spiritual rebirth <note>original: "Regeneration"</note>. However, Adam had not yet reached such a high state; and the fruit of this Tree in this heavenly <note>original: "Aethereal"</note> state of the soul would have been **Immortality** or **Life everlasting**. And the **Tree of the Knowledge of good and evil** was also there—specifically, **his own Will**.

10. And there was a very pleasant River that watered this Garden, which can be divided into four streams. These are the four Cardinal Virtues, which exist in varying degrees in the soul according to the purity of her **Vehicle** <term>The "vehicle of the soul" is a Neoplatonic concept referring to the subtle body or spiritual envelope—ethereal, airy, or physical—that carries the soul through different states of existence.</term>.

11. And the name of the first is **Pison**, which represents **Prudence** and Experience in doing things that are proper. For the soul of man is never idle, neither in this world nor in any other state, but has some duty <note>original: "Province"</note> to fulfill and must promote the interests of the one to whom she belongs. For what greater satisfaction can a good soul have than to be a distributor of some portion of that universal good that God pours out upon the world? And there can be no external social interaction <note>original: "conversation"</note> or society of persons—be they earthly, airy, or heavenly—that does not immediately require the use of **Prudence**. Therefore, **Prudence** is an inseparable accomplishment of the soul. Thus, **Pison** is rightly considered one of the rivers even of that heavenly Paradise. This is that **Wisdom** which God himself shows to the soul by sharing the divine Light; for it is said to encompass the Land of **Havilah**.

12. In that land, idle and useless speculations are not valued, as is clearly shown by the pure and approved **Gold**, **Bdellium**, and **Onyx**—the commodities found there.

13. And the name of the second River is **Gihon**, which is **Justice**, as suggested by the fame of the **Ethiopians** (whose land it is said to encompass) and by the meaning of its name.

14. And the name of the third River is **Hiddekel**, which is **Fortitude**. Like a rapid stream, it sweeps everything before it and stoutly resists all the powers of darkness, running forcefully against **Assyria**, which is situated to its West. And the fourth River is **Perath**, which is **Temperance**, the nourisher and cherisher of all the plants of Paradise. In contrast, **Intemperance**—or dedicating the Mind too much to the pleasures of the **Vehicle** or the physical life <note>original: "Life of the Matter"</note> in any state—drowns and chokes those sacred plants <note>original: "Vegetables"</note>. As you know, the Earth was not fruitful at all until the waters were moved into one place and the dry land appeared; before that, it was drowned and sodden <note>original: "flocken"</note> with too much moisture.

15. In this Paradise thus described, the Lord God had placed Man to tend it and to keep it in the same good order in which he found it.

16. And the Divine Word or Light within man gave him a command, saying: "You may freely eat from every tree of Paradise. For all things here are wholesome as well as pleasant, if you take proper care of yourself and are obedient to my commands."

17. "But you must not eat under any circumstances from the luscious and poisonous fruit of the **Tree of Knowledge of good and evil**—that is, from your **own Will**. For at the time you eat from it, your soul shall contract that languor,"

So far, I have not paid much attention in the **Ethereal Adam** <note>The "Ethereal Adam" represents the human soul in its original, purely spiritual state before it takes on a physical body.</note> to any faculties other than those that carry him upward toward Virtue and the holy **Intellect**. For this faculty enables him to be the head of all living creatures on the earth, just as that faculty is, in fact, the mother of all humanity.

19. I must admit that those higher and more intellectual accomplishments made **Adam** very wise and gave him quick perception. For he knew the natures of the beasts of the field and the birds of the air very well—and I mean not only the visible and earthly creatures, but also the fallen and unfallen angels, or good and bad **spirits** <note>original: "Genii"</note>. He was able to judge them correctly, according to the principles they were made of and the properties they possessed.

20. And his reason and understanding were not mistaken, but he judged everything correctly. However, he could take no such pleasure in God’s external creation and His various works without having some principle of life that could fittingly join with and joyfully animate the same kind of matter they themselves consisted of. Therefore, God endowed the soul of man with a faculty for being united with vital joy and satisfaction to **Matter**, as well as the faculty for aspiring to a union with God Himself (whose Divine Essence is too vastly different from our humble substances). But the **Divine Life** is communicable in some way to both soul and body, whether that body is **ethereal** <note>spiritual or celestial</note> or of a denser consistency. Those wonderful, grateful pleasures that we feel are nothing but the healthy motions of the soul's **Vehicle** <term>In Neoplatonism, the "vehicle" is a subtle, luminous body that acts as an intermediary between the immaterial soul and the physical world.</term>; from this, divine joys themselves are strengthened and enhanced through a kind of reflection. This **Vital Principle**, which joins the soul to the matter of the universe, is of great importance.

21. Therefore God, to satisfy **Adam**, did not make him tireless in his striving toward intellectual things. 3. We are only forbidden to feed on *our own Will*, and to seek pleasures separately and without the approval of the *Will of God*. For if *our own Will* gains dominance within us, we shall assuredly descend into the *Region of Mortality* and be cast into a state of death."

15. And there would be a general hatred and loathing between this *Old Serpent* (as well as all of his fellow rebels) and *mankind*. 16. And concerning *Adam*, the Eternal Lord God decreed that he should descend to become an inhabitant of the Earth. Furthermore, his *feminine part*—his affections and emotions—would be under the discipline and correction of his *Reason*.

Therefore, he called the *life of his vehicle* <note>original: "Life of his Vehicle" — the animating force of his lower, sensory soul that carries it through different states of existence.</note> "EVE," because she is indeed the mother of all generations of people who live upon the Earth.

21. Finally, once the *formative power* <note>original: "Plastick Power" — the natural ability of the soul to unconsciously organize and shape matter into a physical body.</note> was fully awakened, *Adam’s* soul descended into the prepared matter of the Earth. In due time, *Adam* appeared clothed in the skins of beasts; that is, he became a literal *terrestrial animal* and a mortal creature upon the Earth.

22. For the *Eternal God* had decreed it this way, and His wisdom, mercy, and justice (if I may say so) played and worked together in this matter. This was especially so because *Adam* had only rushed himself into a condition that might have eventually fallen to him in the natural course of things anyway. It is appropriate for there to be a leader among the living creatures of the earth like a *terrestrial Adam*, but to live here forever would be to his disadvantage.

23. Therefore, when God removed him from that higher state,

24. He ensured that he would not be immortal. Nor is he capable of reaching the fruit of the *Tree of Life* without first passing through the state of being clothed again in a fiery *vehicle* <note>original: "fiery Vehicle" — a celestial or spiritual body, far more refined than the physical one.</note> and becoming a pure and refined <note>original: "defecate" — meaning purified or cleared of all physical dregs and impurities.</note> *ethereal spirit*. Only then may he be allowed to taste the fruit of the Tree of Life and Immortality, and so live forever.

<summary>Henry More explains the physical descent of Adam into a mortal, "terrestrial" body as the final stage of the Fall, characterizing the "skins of beasts" as the physical human body. He concludes that immortality is only accessible once the soul returns to a refined, ethereal state.</summary>

<meta>This page begins the "Moral Cabbala" section of Henry More’s work. Following the "Philosophic Cabbala" (which dealt with the physical and cosmic creation), this section interprets the Book of Genesis as an allegory for the internal spiritual development of the individual soul. It establishes the "Microcosm" theory—the idea that the human soul contains the same elements and stages of creation as the outer universe.</meta>

### THE
## MORAL
# CABBALA.

## CHAPTER 1.

*1. Man is a microcosm or little world, in whom there are two principles: Spirit and Flesh. 2. The earthly or fleshly nature appears first. 4. The light of conscience is unlistened to. 6. The spirit of intuitive and heartfelt discernment between good and evil. 10. The unruly desires of the flesh are driven aside and limited. 11. Thereupon the plants of righteousness bear fruit and flourish. 16. The hearty and sincere love of God and one's neighbor is like the sun in the soul of man; theoretical knowledge <note>original: "Notionality" — knowledge based on abstract concepts or opinions rather than direct spiritual experience.</note> and opinions are like the weak and faint light of the scattered stars. 18. Those who walk in sincere love walk in the day; those guided by theoretical knowledge travel in the night. 22. The natural desiring faculty <note>original: "Concupiscible" — the part of the soul concerned with physical appetites and desires.</note> brings forth by the command of God and is corrected by devotion. 24. The spirited or aggressive faculty <note>original: "Irascible" — the part of the soul concerned with anger, courage, and self-assertion.</note> also brings forth. 26. Christ, the image of God, is created, being a perfect ruler over all the movements of the aggressive and desiring faculties. 29. The food of the divine life. 30. The food of the animal life. 31. Divine wisdom approves of whatever is simply natural as good.*

We look upon man as a microcosm <note>original: "Microcosm" — a "little world" that mirrors the structure and laws of the entire universe (the macrocosm).</note> or a little world; if he completes the whole progress of the spiritual creation, the process will be understood figuratively as follows. The lesser of these two great Lights has dominion by night and is a rule for those whose inward minds are still held too strongly in the works of darkness. It is a Principle that is weak and variable as the Moon, and it is called *Inconstancy of Life and Knowledge*. There is also an abundance of other little Lights thickly dispersed over the whole Understanding of man, like the Stars in the Firmament, which you may call *Notionality* <note>original: "Notionality" — More uses this to mean a state of having many theoretical ideas or "notions" that have not yet become lived, practical realities.</note>, or a *Multiplicity of ineffectual opinions*.

Thus it is, therefore, that at last God fully manifests the *true* and *perfect Man* in our nature, whereby we ourselves become good and perfect. This person does not only see and love what is good, but has full power to accomplish it in all things: For he has full dominion over the "Fish" of the sea, can rule and guide the "Birds" of the air, and with ease command the "Beasts" of the field, and whatever moves upon the earth.

# The Moral Cabbala. CHAP. II.

1. Thus the Heavenly and Earthly natures in man were finished and fully replenished with all the ornaments belonging to them.

2. So the Divine Wisdom in human nature celebrated her *Sabbath*, having now worked through the labor of all the *six days* of struggle <note>original: "travel" — likely meaning 'travail' or labor/toil</note>.

3. And Divine Wisdom looked upon this *Seventh Day* as blessed and sacred; a day of righteousness, rest, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

4. These were the generations or sproutings <note>original: "Pullulations" — from the Latin *pullulare*, meaning to sprout or bud</note> of the Heavenly and Earthly nature—of the *Divine* and *Animal Life* in man—when *God* created them.

5. I mean those fruitful *plants* and pleasant and useful herbs which he himself planted. For I have described to you the condition of a man taught by God, instructed and nourished by his inward *Light*, where there is no external doctrine to fall like rain, nor any outward gardener to interfere in God’s husbandry.

6. There is only a *fountain of water*, which is *repentance* from dead works, and it bubbles up in the *Earthly Adam* so as to wash all the ground everywhere.

7. And thus, the nature of man being prepared for further achievements, God shapes him into his own *Image*—which is *righteousness* and *true holiness*—and breathes into him the *Spirit of Life*. And this is that *Adam* who is born of *water* and the *Spirit*.

8. So far, I have shown you how mankind is raised up from one degree of spiritual light and righteousness to another, until we finally reach that full command and perfection in the Divine Life, such that a man may be said in some sense to have attained the Kingdom of Heaven or found a Paradise on earth. The narrative that follows shall instruct you and warn you of those evil paths by which man loses that measure of Paradisiacal happiness God grants him <note>original: "estates him in"</note>, even while he is in this world. I say, therefore, that the Lord God planted a garden eastward in *Eden*, and there he put the man whom he had made. That is: a man living under the intellectual rays of the Spirit, being guided by the morning light of the Sun of Righteousness, is led into a very pleasant and sweet contentment of mind, and the testimony of a good conscience is his great delight.

9. And the various sproutings and springings up of the works of righteousness within him are a delightful Paradise to him, pleasing both the sight and the taste of that measure of Divine Life revealed in him. But of all the plants that grow in him, none has such sovereign power as the one in the middle of this garden—namely, the *Tree of Life*, which is *sincere obedience to the Will of God*. Nor does any bear such deadly <note>original: "lethiferous" — from the Latin *lethifer*, meaning death-bearing or fatal</note> and poisonous fruit as the *Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil*, which is *disobedience to the Will of God as it is revealed in man*. For the pleasure of the soul consists in faithfully conforming herself to what she is convinced in her own conscience is the *Will of God*, whatever others might suggest to the contrary.

<meta>This page continues the "Moral Cabbala," an allegorical interpretation of the Garden of Eden. Having established the "Sabbath" of the soul, the author now explains the four rivers of Paradise as the four cardinal virtues and describes the psychological state of "Adam" before the creation of "Eve," representing the balance between intellectual and natural life.</meta>

## CHAP. II. The Moral Cabbala.

10. And all the fruit-bearing trees of righteousness are watered by these four rivers, which wind along this Garden of Pleasure; these are indeed the *four Cardinal Virtues*. <note>The "Cardinal Virtues" are a classical framework of ethics inherited from Greek philosophy: Prudence, Justice, Fortitude, and Temperance.</note>

11. The name of the first is *Pison*, which is *Prudence*. This is not the suggestion of fleshly craft or over-reaching subtlety, but the indications of the Spirit or divine intellect regarding what is fit, profitable, and proper to be done.

12. Here is well-tried and certain approved *Experience*, healthy *Industry*, and an eagerness for honest labor.

13. And the name of the second river is *Gihon*, which is *Justice*.

14. And the name of the third river is *Hiddekel*, which is *Fortitude*; and the fourth river is *Euphrates*, which is *Temperance*.

15. This is the Paradise where the Lord **God** had placed the Man, so that he might further cultivate and improve it.

16. And the Divine Light manifested in the Man encouraged him to eat of the fruits of Paradise freely, and to delight himself in all manner of holy understanding and righteousness.

17. But with all this, He commanded him to take special care regarding how he relished *his own will or power* in anything. Instead, he should be obedient to the manifest will of **God** in things great and small; otherwise, he would assuredly lose the life he then lived and become dead to all righteousness and **Truth**. So the man took special care, and his soul worked wholly toward heavenly and divine things, and heeded nothing but these. His more noble and *Masculine Faculties* <note>In this allegorical system, "Masculine" refers to the rational, intellectual, and divine-oriented powers of the soul.</note> were, in a way, the only ones set to work, while the *Natural Life*—in which there is no sin if it is rightly guided—was almost quite forgotten and disregarded.

18. But the Wisdom of **God** saw that it was not good for the soul of man that its *Masculine Powers* should operate alone. Instead, all the faculties of life should be set in motion, so that the whole of human nature might be fulfilled by the Divine.

19. Now, because the powers of the soul were working so entirely upward toward divine things, the various modifications or shapes of the *Animal Life* <note>The sensory and physical aspects of human existence.</note> were easily discerned for what they were by the man's quick understanding. These aspects of life were represented to him by **God** acting within the framework of human nature, giving him the opportunity to view and judge them. He had a clear and definite understanding of every particular shape of the *Animal Life*.

20. And he judged <note>original: "censure"</note> them or pronounced his opinion of them truly, yet rigidly and severely enough. But as of yet, he was not in a capacity to take any delight in them; none of them were fit to please him.

21. Therefore, Divine Providence brought it to pass—for the good of the man and so that he might be more vigorously and fully enriched with delight—that the operations of the *Masculine Faculties* of the soul were for a while well slackened and lulled to sleep <note>original: "consopited" — from the Latin *consopire*, meaning to put to sleep or quiet</note>. During this time, the faculties themselves were somewhat lessened or weakened, yet in such a due measure and proportion that, considering the future advantage...

25. In this, neither Adam’s Reason nor his Affection had done anything wrong at all; he concluded nothing but what *Divine Wisdom and Fairness* <note>original: "Equity"</note> would approve as true. Therefore, Adam and his wife did not yet seek out corners or hiding places to shelter themselves from the Divine Light; having done nothing wrong, they appeared naked in its presence without any shame or blushing.

<meta>This page continues the "Moral Cabbala," Henry More's allegorical and psychological interpretation of the Book of Genesis. Having previously described the "Creation of Eve" as the emergence of the soul's capacity for physical joy, More now recounts the "Fall of Man" as a psychological event: the moment when the desire for pleasure (the Serpent) overpowers the natural joy of the body (the Feminine part) and lead's the intellect (Adam) into disobedience.</meta>

# CHAPTER III. The Moral Cabbala.

1. **B**ut it so happened that as the *Life of the Body* became so energized in Man, the most cunning and subtle of all the *Animal Configurations*—the *Serpent*, which represents the immoderate *Desire for Pleasure*—craftily worked its way into the *Feminine* part of *Adam*, specifically the *natural joy of the body*. Thus attacking Man, it whispered such suggestions as these to him: "What a rigid and harsh thing is this matter of Religion and the Law of God, as they call it! It robs a man of all kinds of pleasure and cuts him off from all the satisfactions of life."

2. But the *Feminine* <note>original: "Womanish"</note> aspect of *Adam*—that is, the *natural and healthy joy of the body*—could testify against this and replied: "We may take delight in the activities of all the faculties of both Soul and Body that God and Nature have given us.

3. We only need to beware of Disobedience and of following our own *will* indiscriminately. Instead, we must always consult with the *Will of God* and the Divine Light revealed in our understanding, doing all things in an orderly and moderate way. For if we violate this, we shall surely die <note>original: "die the death"</note> and lose the life of Virtue and Righteousness that is now active within us."

4. But the *Serpent*, which is the *inordinate desire for pleasure*, deceived *Adam* through the weakness of his *Feminine Faculties*. It made him believe he would not die, but could safely follow both the free dictates of pleasure (his own will) and the Will of God. It suggested that *Flesh* and *Spirit* could both rule within him without causing any harm <note>original: "prejudice"</note> to each other;

5. and that his skill and experience in the world would be expanded, bringing him closer to Divine Perfection and allowing him to imitate that fullness of Wisdom found in God, who knows all things, whether good or evil.

6. This cunning suggestion so worked its way into *Adam's Feminine Faculties* that his physical *Lust* <note>original: "Concupiscence"</note> grew so strong that it pulled his Will along with it. The whole Man became a lawless and unruly creature. At first glance, it seemed a very pleasant thing to act on whatever our own desires suggest without restraint; it seemed very desirable to try all experiments <note>original: "try all Conclusions"</note> to gain experience and knowledge. But this resulted in nothing but the *wisdom of the flesh* and made *Adam* worldly-minded.

7. But he had not wandered very far in these immoral <note>original: "dissolute"</note> courses before his eyes were opened. He saw the difference—how naked he was now, stripped of all strength and power regarding divine and holy things. He began to think of flimsy excuses for his obvious <note>original: "notorious"</note> folly and disobedience.

8. For the Voice of the Divine Light had come to him in the cool of the day, when the fury and heat of his immoderate passions had somewhat lessened. But *Adam* could not endure its presence and hid himself from it, planning how he should answer with an apology or excuse.

9. But the Divine Light persisted and came closer to him, and

# The Moral Cabbala. CHAPTER III.

9. The Divine Light reproached him, saying that he had become so wild and estranged from the Light itself, demanding to know what condition he was in and why he fled.

10. Then *Adam* sincerely confessed that he found himself in such a pitiful, poor, naked state that he was ashamed to appear in the presence of the Divine Light. He explained that this was the reason he hid himself: because the Light would so clearly reproach him for his nakedness and deformity.

11. And the Divine Light further examined him, asking how he fell into this perceptible, beggarly nakedness. It blamed this sad outcome on his disobedience—the fact that he had fed upon and taken a surfeit <note>original: "surfeit"; an excessive amount or overindulgence</note> of the fruit of his own will.

12. But *Adam* excused his *Rational faculties*, saying they only followed the natural dictates of the *Joy of the Body*—the *Woman* that God himself had given him as a helper and a source of delight.

13. But the Divine Light again blamed *Adam* for not keeping his *Feminine faculties* in better order or subjection, allowing them to so boldly and overwhelmingly dictate things to him that were not fit. To this, he had nothing to say, except that the subtle *Serpent*—the *unrestrained desire for pleasure*—had deceived both his faculties, his *Masculine* as well as his *Feminine*. His Will and Affection were entirely carried away by it.

14. Then the Divine Light began to punish the *Serpent* in *Adam’s* hearing, declaring that it was more accursed than all the other *Animal Figurations* <note>term: More's phrase for the various instincts and drives of the lower soul</note>. It declared that the serpent creeps basely upon its belly, tempting a person toward decadence and lust <note>original: "Riot and Venery"</note>, and relishing nothing but earth and dirt. This will always be its character as long as it lives within a man.

15. But if the Divine Light were to once descend so far into the Man as to take possession of his *Feminine faculties*, it would set the *Natural Joy of the Body* at defiance against the *Serpent*. And though the subtlety of the *Serpent* might slightly wound and disorder the *Woman* for a time, her lawful and free operations—being empowered by divine strength—would afterward completely destroy and extinguish the *Seed of the Serpent*; namely, the *operations of the unrestrained desire for pleasure*.

16. And the Divine Light added further in *Adam's* hearing concerning the *Woman*—as she now stood separated from the heavenly life and was not obedient to right Reason—that by a divine *Nemesis* <note>original: "Nemesis"; here meaning a just and inescapable punishment or divine retribution</note>, she would conceive with sorrow and bring forth futility. Furthermore, her husband—the *Earthly-minded Adam*—would tyrannize over her, weary her out, and defeat her. Thus, the natural <note>original: "kindly"</note> joy of the health and life of the body would be greatly corrupted, or made faint and weak, by the unbridled moods, reckless excess, and intemperance of the *Earthly-minded Adam*.

17. And to *Adam* it said—he who had become so *Earthly-minded* by listening to the voice of his deceived *Woman* and acting disobediently toward the will of God—that his Flesh or "Earth" was accursed for his sake. With labor and toil he would reap its fruits as long as he continued in this *Earthly-mindedness*.

18. It shall also bring forth worries and anxieties for him, and his thoughts shall be as base as those of the animals in the field; he shall think of nothing but what is earthly and sensual.

Dearly embracing the *Joy of his Body*, even though she had grown so disorderly <note>original: "inordinate"</note>, he called her *My Life* <note>original: "Eve," which in Hebrew means "living" or "life-giver"</note>, professing she was the nursing mother and chief comfort of all men living, and that none could survive without her.

21. Then Divine Wisdom put hairy coats made of the skins of wild beasts upon *Adam* and his *Wife*, and deservedly reproached them, saying, "Now get you gone, you couple of brutes." And *Adam* would have very gladly escaped that way, if he could, and settled forever in that bestial nature.

22. But the Eternal God of heaven, whose providence reaches to all things and whose mercy is over all his works, looking upon *Adam*, perceived what a pitiful, ridiculous case he was in; who, seeking to be like God in knowledge and freedom, made himself no better than a beast, and would have willingly lived forever in that lower kind of nature. Therefore the Eternal Lord God, in compassion to *Adam*, designed the contrary; and deriding his boldness and curiosity that made him transgress, "Behold," says he, "*Adam* has become like one of us, knowing Good and Evil; and can of himself enlarge his pleasure and create new paradises of his own, which forsooth must also have their *Tree of Life* or *Immortality*." For *Adam* would have lived forever in this foolish state he had placed himself in.

23. But the Eternal Lord God would not suffer *Adam* to settle into the bestial delight which he had chosen, but drove him out of this false *Paradise* which he would have made for himself, and set him to cultivate his *fleshly members*, out of which his *earthly-mindedness* was taken.

24. I say, he forcibly drove out *Adam* from this *Paradise of Luxury*; nor could he settle perpetually in the brutish life, because the *Cherubim* with the flaming sword that turned every way beat him off; that is, the *manly faculties of Reason and Conscience* met him ever and anon in his brutish purposes, and convinced him so of his folly that he could not find rest forever in this bestial condition.

<meta>This page continues the preface to Henry More’s "The Defense of the Threefold Cabbala," where he anticipates and addresses potential criticisms of his philosophical interpretation of the Book of Genesis.</meta>

->READER,<-

The *Cabbalas* <note>original: "Cabbala"—a Jewish mystical and philosophical tradition of interpreting the Bible; here, More refers to his own "threefold" version.</note> you have read are likely so strange and unexpected—especially the *Philosophical* one—that I thought it best to interrupt you for a moment. I want to ensure that the *Defense* itself, which is meant to cure and stop your amazement, does not cause further doubt or offense in any of its passages. I hope that whatever I suspect may not satisfy you will be strengthened in advance by this short *Preface*.

For my part, I cannot predict what any person might reasonably object to, unless it be: *the unusual Mystery of Numbers*; *the use of Heathen <note>original: "Heathen"—referring here to non-Christian, specifically ancient Greek, philosophers.</note> authority to explain Scripture*; *the addition of miracles performed by them to further confirm their authority*; and finally, *the strangeness of the philosophical conclusions themselves*.

<margin>He [Abraham] granted them arithmetic and handed over matters concerning astronomy. Josephus, *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 1, Chapter 9. <note>original Greek: Τήν τε Ἀριθμητικὴν αὐτοῖς χαρίζεται, καὶ τὰ περὶ ἀστρονομίαν παραδίδωσι.</note></margin>
Regarding the *Mystery of Numbers*, the idea that this ancient *philosophy* of *Moses* should be wrapped up in it will not seem unlikely if we consider that the *Cabbala* of the *Creation* was preserved in the hands of *Abraham* and his family. Abraham was famous for *Mathematics* (of which *Arithmetic* is a necessary part), first among the *Chaldeans*, and afterward, as *historians* write, he taught the same *arts* to the *Egyptians*. Besides *prophetic* and *riddling* <note>original: "Ænigmatical"</note> writings, it is well known—even in the *Scriptures themselves*—that authors often hide their *secrets* using *names*, *etymologies*, and the symbolism of *numbers*. This needs no proof; I will only point to that one famous example: the number of the *Beast, 666*.

As for citing *Heathen writers* so frequently: you should consider that these are the *wisest* and the *most virtuous* among them. They are either those whom the *Church Fathers* say received their *philosophy* from *Moses* and the *Prophets*—such as *Pythagoras* and *Plato*—or they are the *disciples* or *friends* of these *philosophers*. Therefore, I thought it very appropriate to use their *testimony* for a subject they seemed well-qualified to witness, having received the *Cabbala* from the ancient *prophets*. I will not deny that they have mixed their own foolishness into it, either through a wild *imagination* or a mistake of *judgment*. Examples include the *reincarnation of human souls into animals* <note>original: "Transmigration of Humane Souls into Brutes"</note>; *complete abstinence from meat*; *too severe a rejection of bodily pleasures*; *the disparagement of marriage*, and similar ideas. However, these are no more an *argument* against the main purpose of the *Cabbala* than the unjustifiable superstitious *opinions* and *practices* of some misguided *churches* are against the solid foundations of *Christianity*.

Again, I do not cite *philosophers* alone. As the occasion requires, I also cite the *Church Fathers* and—what I believe to be just as valid in this case—the *Jewish Rabbins* <note>original: "Rabbins"—Rabbis.</note>, who,

# The PREFACE

...who, in things where prejudice need not blind them, I should think as fit as any to confirm a Cabbalistic sense, especially if there is a general consent among them, and that they do not write their own private fancy, but the mind of their whole Church.

Now if anyone takes offense at the scholars of Pythagoras swearing, as is believed, by their Master who taught them the mystery of the *Tetractys* <term>Tetractys: A mystical symbol consisting of ten dots arranged in a triangle, representing the number four and symbolizing the organization of the universe.</term> (as you shall understand more fully in the *Explication of the Fourth day’s work*), I must profess that I myself am not a little offended by it. But that high reverence they bore to Pythagoras, while it is a sign of vanity and a kind of superstition in them, is also no less an argument for a stupendous measure of knowledge and sanctity in Pythagoras himself, that he should draw such great honor from them, and that his memory should be so sacred to them. He acquired this profound knowledge and sanctity by conversing with the Jewish Prophets; this ultimately tends to the renown of that Church, and consequently to the Christian Church, which inherits those holy Oracles <note>original: "Oracles"—the divinely inspired scriptures.</note> which were first unique to the Jews.

<margin>See the Appendix to the *Defense of the Philosophical Cabbala*, chapter 2, section 3.</margin>

But the transgressions of Pythagoras's followers are no more to be imputed to him than the superstitions directed toward the Virgin Mary can be laid to her charge. Besides, it may be a question whether in that Pythagorean Oath, *"No, by him..."* <note>original Greek: Οὐ μὰ τὸν... — the beginning of the oath "No, by him who gave to our soul the Tetractys."</note> etc., they did not actually swear by God, the first Author of the Cabbala and that mysterious explanation of the Tetractys—that is, indeed, of all knowledge divine and natural—who first gave it to Adam and then revived or confirmed it again to Moses. Or if it must be understood as referring to Pythagoras, why may it not be looked upon as a civil oath or solemn statement, such as Joseph swearing by the *Life of Pharaoh*, or noblemen by their *Honors*? Neither of these, for my own part, can I allow, or be certain that they are merely civil; rather, they touch upon religion, or rather, idolatrous superstition.

<margin>Iamblichus, *On the Life of Pythagoras*, chapter 13.</margin>

As for the miracles Pythagoras performed, though I do not believe all that are recorded of him are true, I hold those that I have recited to be probable enough, as they are not unbecoming of the person's worth. But those stories that suggest the *transmigration* <term>transmigration: the belief that a soul passes into another body after death, particularly into an animal.</term> of human souls into the bodies of beasts, I look upon as fables; and his *whispering into the ear of an ox* to tell it to stop eating beans, I consider a blatant lie. But it seems very consistent with Divine Providence that Pythagoras, having gained the knowledge of the holy Cabbala which God imparted to Adam and Moses, should be empowered to perform miracles to give it credibility among the nations. For in this way, those noble and ancient truths were more firmly rooted among the philosophers of Greece and happily preserved to this very day.

<margin>
Iamblichus, *On the Life of Pythagoras*, chapter 28.
*History of Bel and the Dragon* (Apocrypha).
Acts 8:39, 40.
</margin>

Nor can his being *carried through the air* <note>original: "carried in the Air"—referring to legends of Pythagoras being seen in distant places or transported miraculously.</note> make him suspected of being a mere magician or conjurer, since the holy Prophets and Apostles themselves have been transported in that manner; such as Habakkuk from Judea <note>original: "Jewry"</note> to Babylon, and Philip, after he had baptized the Eunuch, from between Gaza and Jerusalem to Azotus. But for my own part, I think the working of miracles is one of the least perfections of a man, and contributes nothing at all to the happiness of the person who performs them—or rather, seems to perform them. For if they are true miracles, he does not do them, but some other Power or Person distinct from him. And yet here magicians and witches are greatly delighted in that this...

# To the READER

**Power** is in some way attributed to such people, and they are admired by the public, as is clearly seen in the case of **Simon Magus** <note>Simon Magus: A figure from the New Testament (Acts 8) who practiced sorcery and was often cited by early modern writers as the archetype of the "false" miracle-worker motivated by pride.</note>. But to rule and dominate through the attribute of **Power** alongside the **Prince of the Air** <note>Prince of the Air: A biblical title for Satan (Ephesians 2:2), implying that seeking power for the sake of status is a devilish trait.</note>—what is that but mere **Pride**, the most irrational and provoking **Vice** there is? 

And with what gross folly is it joined here! They take pride and pleasure in the fact that they sometimes do—or rather, undergo—what **herons** and **wild geese**, and every ordinary **bird** can do on its own: that is, mount high and glide through the shifting **Air**. But **Holy** and **Good** people know that the greatest **Sweetness** and **Perfection** of a **Virtuous** soul is the natural fulfillment of her own nature in true **Wisdom** and divine **Love**. If anything miraculous happens to them, or is performed by them, it is so that the worth and knowledge within them might be noticed, and that **God** may be glorified as they act as His witnesses. No other increase in **Happiness** comes to them from this, except that they are now better able to make others happy; I believe this was the case for **Pythagoras**.

To ensure that people do not indulge too much in their own **Melancholy** <note>original: "Melancholy"—in this era, melancholy was considered a physical humor that, when imbalanced, could cause delusions or "false inspirations."</note> and **Fancy**, which they usually call **Inspiration**: if they truly are such great lights to the world as they claim, and so high that they will not stoop to the examination of human **Reason**, it would be desirable for such people to keep their heat inside to digest the raw ideas <note>original: "concoct the crudities"—a metaphor from digestion, meaning to refine or process unformed thoughts.</note> of their own thoughts until the authority of a **Miracle** calls them out. In that way, they might more rightfully claim the people's attention, being authorized from above to tell us something we did not know before—and which we can only believe rather than fully know—since the main argument is not **Reason**, but a **Miracle**.

Lastly, regarding the **Strangeness** of the **Philosophical Conclusions** themselves: it would be the strangest thing of all if they did not seem very **Paradoxical** and strange at first glance. Otherwise, why should they be hidden and concealed from the **common people** <term>the Vulgar: The general public or those without specialized philosophical training.</term>, except that they surpassed their capacity and were far out of proportion to what they could believe? 

But on behalf of these **Cabbalistic Conclusions** <note>original: "Cabbalistical"—referring here to More's belief in an ancient, secret tradition of divinely inspired philosophy.</note>, I will only note this much: assuming they are true (which I will only assert until a capable **Philosopher** or **Theologian** proves them false), there is nothing of significant importance in **Theology** or **Nature** that cannot be easily explained by this **Hypothesis**. An eminent part of this includes the **Motion of the Earth** <note>The "Motion of the Earth" refers to the Copernican theory that the Earth revolves around the sun, which was still a point of debate in the 17th century.</note> and the **Preexistence of Souls**. The evidence for the former truth is such that it has won the agreement of the most famous **Mathematicians** of recent times; and the reasonableness of the latter is no less certain. Indeed, there has never been any philosopher who held the **Soul** of **Man** to be immortal who did not also hold that it **preexisted** the body.

However, **Religion** is not eager to expose the full view of **Truth** to the people, but only what is most necessary to keep them in the fear of a **Deity** and obedience to the **Law**. She contented herself with what merely concerned the state of the **Soul** after the death of the **Body**, concealing whatever could be imagined concerning her condition before then. 

Now, I say, it is a remarkable quality of Falsehood (if this **Hypothesis** is false) and very noteworthy that it should better suit the **Attributes of God**, the visible events of **Providence**, the **Phenomena of Nature**, the **Reason** of **Man**, and the

# The PREFACE.

...the holy Text itself, where people acknowledge a mysterious **Cabbala** <note>Cabbala: Historically referring to Jewish mystical tradition, More uses it here to describe a deeper, symbolic interpretation of the Bible as opposed to a strictly literal one.</note>, than that which by all means must be accounted true: namely, *that there is no such motion of the earth about the sun, nor any preexistence of human souls.*

<margin>Aristotle, *Metaphysics*, Book 2, chapter 3.</margin>
Reader, I have done my part so that you may read this defense of mine without any obstacle or stumbling. Let me now request only one thing which you are bound to grant: that you read my defense without prejudice, and that all along as you go, you do not refer back to the customary ideas of your imagination, but consult with your free reason, "for the accustomed is more familiar," as **Aristotle** speaks in his *Metaphysics* <note>original: "τὸ γὰρ σύνηθες γνωριμώτερον" (to gar synēthes gnōrimōteron)</note>. For custom is a second nature; and therefore we unknowingly appeal to those ideas that are customary and familiar as if they were indeed the *natural light of the mind* and its *first common notions*. And he gives an example not entirely unsuitable to our present purpose: "How much power custom holds is shown by the laws, in which the mythical and childish elements prevail more than the knowledge about them, because of habit" <note>original: "Ἡλίκην δ’ ἰσχὺν ἔχει τὸ σύνηθες οἱ νόμοι δηλῶσιν, ἐν οἷς τὰ μυθώδη καὶ παιδαριώδη μεῖζον ἰσχύει τοῦ γινώσκειν περὶ αὐτῶν διὰ τὸ ἔθος" (Hēlikēn d' ischyn echei to synēthes hoi nomoi dēlousin...)</note>. The philosopher may be as bold as he pleases with the ritual laws and religious stories of the heathens, but I do not know that he was ever acquainted with the Law of **Moses**. Yet I think I may say—not without due reverence—that there is something of **Aristotle’s** saying analogically true in the very history of the creation; the first impressions of the *literal text*, which is so plainly adapted to the capacity of mere children and unlearned people <term>Idiots: In the 17th century, "idiot" referred to an uneducated or common person lacking specialized knowledge, rather than being a modern slur.</term>, have, because of custom, so strongly rooted themselves in the minds of some that they take that literal sense to be more true than the true meaning of the text itself.

<margin>
Lactantius, *Divine Institutes*, Book 3, chapter 24.
See also José de Acosta, *Natural and Moral History of the Indies*, Book 1.
</margin>
This is clear in a person no less significant than one of the Church Fathers, namely **Lactantius** <note>Lactantius (c. 250 – c. 325): An early Christian author whose literal interpretation of the Bible led him to reject the idea of a spherical earth.</note>, who, looking upon the world as a *tent* according to the description in the *literal Cabbala*, did very stoutly and confidently deny the existence of the **Antipodes** <term>Antipodes: People living on the opposite side of the globe.</term>. In this, a customary imagination prevailed over the free use of his reason.

I thought it appropriate to provide this preface as a warning. As for the rest—the introduction to the defense and the very structure and nature of the defense itself—I hope they will satisfy the judicious and open-minded reader.

By acting according to his precepts, they would simply prove themselves to be *cosmopolitans—true citizens of the world and loyal subjects to God and Nature*. This is Philo’s <note>Philo of Alexandria, a Jewish philosopher who sought to harmonize the Torah with Greek philosophy</note> interpretation of the passage. Another equally significant reason why that holy and wise lawgiver, Moses, should begin with the Creation of the world is this: the laws and ordinances which he gave to the Israelites were presented by him as *God-given* <note>original Greek: Θεοπαράδοτα (theoparadota)</note>, as statutes received directly from God. Therefore, the primary argument and incentive for obedience should rest in this first and highest Lawgiver: God Himself, the great Jehovah. His wisdom, power, and goodness could not be better displayed than by ascribing the creation of the entire visible world to Him. Thus, He might be feared for His power, admired for His wisdom, and finally, loved, adored, and honored as God <note>original: "Deified"</note> for His goodness. Just as He was truly the Most High God in Himself, so He should be acknowledged as such by the people.

For certainly nothing so captures—or even ravishes and carries captive—the minds of poor mankind as bounty and generosity <note>original: "Munificence"</note>. All people love themselves most affectionately, and most of all those with the lowest and meanest spirits. Their souls are so far from being even slightly raised or released from self-interest that they desperately and impulsively cling to their own physical bodies <note>original: "dear carkaſes"</note>. Because they so strongly relish the pleasures and conveniences of life, they have had no qualms about honoring as gods those who, through industry or good luck, produced anything that improved the happiness and comfort of the body.

3. This is why the Sun and Moon were considered the two primary deities by idolatrous antiquity—namely, because of the tangible <note>original: "sensible"</note> benefits they bestowed upon hungry mankind. The one waters the earth, as it were, through her moist influence; the other ripens the fruit of the ground with his warm rays and reveals daily all the hidden treasures of the visible world by his glorious approach, pleasing the sight with the variety of nature's objects and cheering the whole body with his comfortable heat. To these, as the most conspicuous benefactors of mankind, the name *God* <note>original Greek: Θεὸς (Theos)</note> was given, from the word meaning "to run" <note>original Greek: παρὰ τὸ θέειν (para to theein)</note>, because they observed that these supposed deities were in perpetual motion.

These two are the Egyptians' Osiris and Isis. Five others are added to them as very significant benefactors, but subordinate to and dependent on the first two. In plain speech, these are *Fire, Spirit, Humidity, Dryness <note>original: "Siccity"</note>, and Air*; but in their divine titles, they are *Vulcan, Jupiter, Oceanus, Ceres, and Minerva*.

<meta>This page continues the Introduction to "The Defence," where More discusses why Moses chose to open the scriptures with an account of the Creation. He argues that this was a strategic and compassionate choice to lead people away from idolizing physical pleasures and toward the worship of the true Creator.</meta>

# The Introduction to the Defence.

...two for instance, *Bacchus* and *Ceres*, the one the inventor of *corn*, the other of *wine* and *beer*. So it may all be boiled down to that brutish aphorism:

->For that which nourishes me, that I take to be a god. <note>original Greek: Τὸ γὰρ τρέφον με τᾶτ' ἐγὼ οἶμαι θεόν.</note><-

That which could please or satisfy degenerate mankind in their physical bodies—they having lost the image of God in their souls and become like mere animals—that thing must be their god.

Therefore, it was necessary for *Moses*, having to deal with such earthly spirits, children of sense and physical form, to propose *Jehovah* to them as the Maker of this perceptible and physical world. He did this so that whatever sweetness they draw out of its various parts, they might attribute to Him as the first Fountain and Author, without whom neither they nor anything else would have existed. By this, they might be moved to praise His name and fulfill His will, as revealed to them by His servant *Moses*. This was a true and sound wisdom, aiming at nothing but the glory of God and the benefit of these poor, ignorant people.

5. And from this same principle springs the manner of his delivery of the Creation story. That is, it is adapted to the understanding of even the simplest person. He does not speak of things according to their *very essence* and *real nature*, but according to how they *appear to us*. He does not raise high and complex questions or conclude them with subtle arguments. Instead, he sets out the Creation in a familiar and condescending <note>In this context, "condescending" means "lowering oneself to another's level" in a helpful way, rather than being insulting.</note> way, according to the most easy and obvious concepts the people themselves had of the things they saw in the world. He even omitted those more dense things hidden in the depths of the earth, such as metals and minerals, as well as those things that cannot be sensed at all, such as immaterial substances, angels, or celestial intelligences. Thus, the wisdom and goodness of God has fitly adapted the outward <term>cortex</term> <note>original: "cortex," meaning the outer shell or literal layer of a text.</note> of the Scripture to the very narrow and slow understanding of the common people.

Nor does it follow that the narrative must be untrue just because it is written according to the *appearance* of things to the senses and common imagination. For there is also a *truth of appearance*, according to which Scripture mostly speaks when dealing with *philosophical* matters.

And this position is the main key, as I believe—and I hope I shall hereafter plainly prove—by which *Moses's* *Bereshith* <note>original: "Bereshith," the Hebrew title of Genesis, meaning "In the beginning."</note> may, according to the outward and *literal sense*, be understood without any difficulty or conflict between one part and another.

<margin>*Rabbi Maimonides, The Guide for the Perplexed, part 1, chapter 26.*</margin>
First, therefore, I say that it is a thing confessed by the learned *Hebrews*, who make it a rule for understanding many places of Scripture: *The Law speaks according to human language* <note>original Latin: "Loquitur lex juxta linguam humanam."</note>.

And secondly—which will bring us closer to the point—I shall provide examples of some places that must, of necessity, be understood this way:
*Genesis 19:23*: *The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot entered into Zoar*; which implies that the sun was previously *under the earth*, which is true only according to our senses and <term>common imagination</term> <note>original: "vulgar Fancie."</note>.

Or the **ultimate limit** <note>original Latin: *Non plus ultra*</note>: As it is obvious to those who understand the natural meaning of **"end"** <note>original Hebrew: קצה (*qatseh*)</note> and **"extremity"** <note>original Greek: ἄκρον (*akron*)</note>; for those words plainly describe the Earth as being bounded by the blue Heavens, and the Heavens bounded by the horizon of the Earth, with the two touching one another. This is true only to our **senses** and **in appearance**, as any person who is not a total simpleton will admit.

*Ecclesiasticus 27:12. The conversation of a godly man is always filled with wisdom, but a fool changes like the Moon.* This is to be understood according to **sensory appearance**: For if a fool changed no more than the Moon actually does in reality, he would be a wise and excellently accomplished man; **always the same** <note>original Latin: *Semper idem*</note>, though he appears different to the sight of ordinary people. In reality, at least one hemisphere of the Moon is always illuminated, even when she is least visible to us.

Another example can be found in *2 Chronicles 4:2. He also made a cast metal Sea <note>The "Sea" was a massive bronze basin used for ritual washing in Solomon's Temple.</note> ten cubits from brim to brim, perfectly round, and five cubits high; a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.* This is a physical impossibility, as the diameter cannot be ten cubits if the circumference is only thirty <note>Mathematically, the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 10 is approximately 31.4 cubits (using pi). The Bible provides a rounded figure of 30.</note>. But it pleases the Spirit of God here to speak according to the common habits and opinions of men, rather than the mathematical precision of **Archimedes'** proofs.

Again, in *Psalm 19: In the heavens God has set a tent for the sun, which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, and rejoices like a strong man to run his race.* As **John Calvin** <note>A prominent 16th-century theologian and leader in the Protestant Reformation.</note> observes, this is spoken according to the simple understanding of the common people, whom **David** would have struggled in vain to teach the mysteries of Astronomy. Therefore, he makes no mention of the Sun's path through the night sky on the other side of the world.

Add to these *Joshua 10:12: Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and you Moon, in the Valley of Ajalon;* where it is obvious that **Joshua** does not speak according to astronomical truth, but according to **sensory appearance**. For even if the **Sun** and **Moon** were positioned at the best possible advantage without leaving their natural orbits, they were actually so far from being directly over **Ajalon** and **Gibeon** that they were, in truth, many hundreds of miles away from them. And if the Sun and Moon were on the other side of the **equator**, that distance might amount to thousands.

Lastly (and there is nothing more important to consider), the literal text of the Scripture limits the height of the World to the **clouds**, or thereabouts, as is very apparent:

First, because the **clouds** are described as the place where God lives; therefore, we are meant to assume they are placed at the highest point. There He lives, runs, rides, and walks. *He came walking upon the wings of the wind*, in *Psalm 104: Who lays the beams of his chambers in the waters, who makes the clouds his chariot, and walks on the wings of the wind.* He *lays the beams of His chambers in the waters*—meaning the **upper waters**, which are the **clouds**. Therefore, according to the literal text, the Almighty’s lodgings are located in the **clouds**.

That area is also His field for exercise and war: *Deuteronomy 33:26. There is none like the God of Jeshurun <note>A poetic name for the people of Israel.</note>, who rides upon the Heavens for your help*

help in his excellence on the sky—that is, upon the *Upper clouds*, as *Buxtorf* <note>Johannes Buxtorf (1564–1629) was a celebrated German scholar of Hebrew.</note> interprets it. Indeed, what can *shachaqim* <note>Hebrew: שחקים</note> properly signify in this context but *Clouds*? For below, on earth, the word signifies *very fine dust* <note>original Latin: *pulvis tenuissimus*</note>, and the *Clouds* are, as it were, the dust of heaven. *Vatable* <note>François Vatable (died 1547) was a renowned French humanist and Hebraist.</note> also interprets that passage as God riding on the Clouds. This agrees well with Nahum 1:3: *The Lord has his way in the whirlwind, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.* Here he is running as swift as a whirlwind and raises a dust of clouds about him.

You shall find him riding again in Psalm 68:4, and that in triumph—yet only *on the Clouds* (fitting with the passage in *Deuteronomy*): *Sing to God, sing praises to his Name, extol Him who rides upon the Heavens by his name JAH, and rejoice before Him.* The phrase "that rides upon the Heavens" in Hebrew is *larokheb ba-araboth* <note>Hebrew: לרוכב בערבות</note>. I would be bold enough—with *Aben Ezra’s* <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167) was a distinguished Jewish scholar, astronomer, and biblical commentator.</note> permission—to translate this as *he who rides upon the Clouds*. Clouds cause darkness, and the root word from which *araboth* comes is *erebh* <note>Hebrew: ערב</note>, which means *to be darkened* or *to be obscured* <note>original Latin: *obtenebrari, obscurari*</note>. As for the basis of the Rabbi's interpretation ("Upon the heavens"), it is taken from the 33rd verse of Psalm 68: *To him who rides upon the Heavens of heavens of old*. 

But if we continue reading there, we shall find that those *Heavens of heavens*, in all probability, reach no higher than the *Clouds*. Let us read the whole verse together: *To him who rides upon the Heavens of heavens that were of old; look, he sends out his voice, and that a mighty voice.* What is that but *Thunder*? And where does *Thunder* come from but out of the *Clouds*? And where then does God ride but on the *Clouds*? The following verse makes it all plain: *Ascribe strength to God; His excellence is over Israel, and his strength is in the clouds.* This notably confirms that the extent of the Heavens, according to the literal words of *Moses* and *David* as well, reaches only to about the height of the clouds. For here the "Heaven of heavens" is the seat of *Thunder*, and God’s strength and power are said to be in the *Clouds*. Nor does this expression of height—namely, *the Heaven of heavens of old*—imply any further distance. Since the whole Firmament, from the lower waters to the upper waters, is called *Heaven*, it is not at all unreasonable that the highest part of this Heaven or Firmament be called the "Heaven of Heavens." This is my first argument: that the extent of the Heaven or Firmament is only from the sea to the clouds, according to the common phrasing of Scripture—namely, because God is seated no higher.

My second argument is taken from the way the *Heavens* and the *Clouds* are joined together interpretively, one with another, to describe something that is exceedingly high—as high as we can express. The Psalmist does this often. Psalm 36:5: *Your mercy, O Lord, is in the Heavens, and your faithfulness reaches to the Clouds.* And Psalm 57:10: *For your mercy is great to the Heavens, and your truth to the Clouds.* And Psalm 108:4: *For your mercy is great above the Heavens, and your truth reaches above the Clouds.* In these passages, *Heaven* and *Clouds* represent one and the same height, which is used to symbolize the vastness of God's mercy and truth.

My last argument comes from the Psalmist's placement of the Sun *ba-shachaq* <note>Hebrew: בשחק</note>—in the clouds, or in the cloudy heaven. For the word must have this meaning, as I proved above through scholarly testimony, and could also prove from its etymology...

For *shachaq* <note>Hebrew: שחק</note> signifies "to crush" or "to beat into small pieces" <note>original Latin: *comminuere, contundere*</note>, to beat into dust: and what are *Clouds* but the *dust* of heaven, so to speak? *Psalm* 89:36–37: *His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the Sun before me: It shall be established for ever as the Moon, and as the faithful witness in the sky* <note>original Hebrew: בשחק, *ba-shachaq*</note>: that is, in the sky, the place where the clouds are. The drawing down, therefore, of the *Sun*—that faithful witness in heaven—so low as the *Clouds*, implies that the literal text of the Scripture takes no notice of any significant part of the Firmament above the clouds. It always limits its expressions to that *extent*. And this suits very well with *Moses* calling the Sun and the Moon the *great lights*, while making nothing, as it were, of the stars; as is manifest from the 16th verse of the first chapter of *Genesis*: *And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; He made the stars also.* But the stars are included as if they were thrown into the bargain, as if they were not very significant; whereas, in fact, a star of the first magnitude is (according to the calculations of astronomers) twenty thousand times larger than the *Earth*, and the *Earth* is forty-five times larger than the *Moon*. Thus, one *star* of the first magnitude will prove to be about nine hundred thousand times larger than the *Moon*. Despite this, according to the literal word of *Moses*, the Moon is one of the *two great lights*, the sole empress of the night.

But here the literal word of *Moses* is very consistent with itself: for since the *extent* of heaven is not acknowledged any higher than the clouds, or thereabouts (where, as I showed you, the *Sun* is, and consequently the *Moon*), it will not be any more harsh to make the *stars* stoop so low too. Indeed, they must of necessity all be that low, having nowhere else to be higher according to the usual phrasing of Scripture. The appearances of them all to our sight will sufficiently establish their proportions to one another; and the *Sun* and the *Moon* (according to this hypothesis) will prove to be the *two great lights*, and the stars merely scattered sky-pebbles. Therefore, from all this harmony and correspondence of things, I think I may safely conclude *that the extent of the Firmament, according to Moses, is only the distance from the sea to the clouds, or thereabouts, just as it appears to our sight, which cannot discern any interval of altitude between the clouds and the Moon, the Moon and the Sun, and lastly between the Sun and the fixed stars.*

I might add to these proofs the support of many Church Fathers and modern theologians, such as *Chrysostom*, *Ambrose*, *Augustine*, *Bernard*, *Aquinas*, and the rest. But it is already manifest enough *that the Scripture speaks not according to the exact precision of truth, describing things according to their very nature and essence* <note>original Greek: καθ’ οὐσίαν, *kath’ ousian*</note>; *but according to their appearance to the senses and common opinion* <note>original Greek: κατ’ ἔμφασιν, *kat’ emphasin*</note>.
