# The Defense of the Moral Cabbala. CHAP. III.

When she <note>The "Divine Life" or "Divine Love" personified as a feminine figure, similar to the biblical portrayal of Wisdom.</note> plays with ease within her own pure and undisturbed light, she is most lovely and amiable. If she steps out into zeal, satirical rebuke, and contention, it is a condescension <note>original: "condescent"; here meaning a lowering of herself or a temporary departure from her natural state of peace.</note> and a debasement for the present. However, the purpose is a more enlarged exaltation of her own nature, and the gaining of a more universal foothold in other persons by dislodging her deformed enemy.

For **divine Love** is the love of **divine Beauty**, and that **Beauty** is the **divine Life** which would gladly infuse itself and become one with that particular principle of natural life: the soul of man. Whatever person she has taken hold upon and won to herself, she so activates and guides that she makes use of everything he possesses. She improves it for her own **interest**, which is the advancement of herself.

But she observes that her progress and speed are not as fast as she could wish—that is, that mankind is not made as fully and as generally happy by her as she desires and as they are capable of being. Therefore, she raises in a man his anger and indignation against those things that are obstacles and impediments in her way. She beats down with solid reason such things that merely pretend to be reasonable. She also strikes down things that are neither the genuine offspring of human faculties nor the effects of her own union with them. She discounts and derides them as monsters and mixed <note>original: "Mongrel"; referring to ideas or behaviors that are unnatural hybrids of human error rather than pure divine or human nature.</note> things, as they are neither a fulfillment of human nature nor any gift of the divine. 

She also observes that mankind is recklessly busy in trying to improve their natural faculties without her, promising themselves extraordinary results from their own skill and industry. If they could bring these to pass, they would in the end be nothing but a scourge and plague to them. Such efforts would only make them more desperately bold, sensual, atheistical, and wicked—for no fire but that of God's Spirit in a man can clear up the true knowledge of himself to us. She therefore takes courage, even though she sees herself slighted or unknown, and deservedly magnifies herself above all the effects of human art and industry. She boldly tells the world what petty and poor things they are when compared to her.

Nor does she at all hesitate to pour out her full scorn and derision upon those gaudy effects of fanatical fancy, where **melancholy** <note>In the 17th century, "melancholy" was considered a physical ailment of the "black bile" that could cause delusions, hallucinations, or "fanatical" religious visions.</note> dictates strange and uncouth dreams out of a dark hole, like the whispers of the **heathen oracles**. It is not only an injury to herself that such **grotesque fantasies** <note>original: "Antick Phantasms"</note> are preferred over the pure simplicity of her own beauty, but it is a great mischief to her darling—the soul of man. She is grieved that he should forsake those faculties she intends to sanctify and take into herself, and instead give himself up to mere inconsiderate imaginations and accidental impressions. He chooses them for his guide simply because they are the strongest feelings, not the truest, and he will not even examine them.

Occasions such as these, and several others, oftentimes shape the **divine life** in good men and sharpen it into a high degree of zeal and anger. But even those whom she wounds in her wrath, she pities, as she is an affectionate lover of all mankind, even though she is an irreconcilable enemy of their vices.

I have now gone through my *Threefold Cabbala* <note>original: "Cabbala"; here referring to More's three-part interpretation (Literal, Philosophical, and Moral) of the first chapters of Genesis.</note>, which I hope all sincere and judicious Christians will receive with unprejudiced candor and kind acceptance. For just as I have vividly set out the mysteries of the holy and precious life of a Christian, even within the *Mosaical Letter* <note>The literal text of the Books of Moses (the Pentateuch).</note>, I have also carefully and intentionally cleared and defended the grand essential principles of Christianity itself as a specific *religion*. 

In doing so, I have avoided that "rock of offense" which some—who are considered significant lights in the *Christian* world—have placed before men. These individuals thin everything out into *allegories* to such an extent that they leave the very fundamentals of religion suspect. Most notably, they do not even deign to acknowledge that the *Person of Christ* still exists, much less that he is a *Mediator with God for us*, or that he was a *sacrifice for sin* when he hung on the cross at *Jerusalem*. They even doubt that he will appear again in the *heavens*, as was promised by the two angels to his Apostles who saw him ascend, or that there is any *life to come* after the dissolution of the natural body. This is despite our Savior Christ expressly saying, *That after the Resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like the angels of God*. 

To be so "spiritual" as to interpret this as a *mysterious resurrection* of a man within this life is, in effect, to be so truly carnal as to insinuate there is no such thing at all as the *life to come*. It adds to *Sadducism* <note>The beliefs of the Sadducees, a Jewish sect known for denying the resurrection of the dead.</note> a form of *Epicurism* <note>Refers here to the pursuit of physical pleasure and the denial of divine providence or judgment.</note>—or worse. That is, it creates a "religious liberty" to fill one another's houses with illegitimate children from adulterous beds, under the pretense that they have now "risen" to a state where they may blamelessly commit what is, for other mortals, outright *adultery*. Such unlawful playing with the *Literal* text is, to me, no sign of a *spiritual man*. Rather, it marks someone who is at least indiscreet and light-minded—more gross, in my opinion, than *Hymeneus* and *Philetus* <note>Two early Christians mentioned in 2 Timothy 2:17-18 who claimed the resurrection had already happened, thereby undermining the faith of others.</note>, who also claimed the resurrection was already past and so used allegory to destroy the faith of the people.

For my own part, I cannot admire any man's *fancies*, but only his *reason*, *modesty*, *discretion*, and *miracles*—the main requirement being presupposed (which is the birthright of even the humblest *Christian*) that he be *truly and sincerely pious*. But if his imagination grows rampant and he aspires to appear as some strange thing in the world, the likes of which has never been heard of, that man seems to me to plainly reveal his own *carnality* and *ignorance*. For there are no better truths than those already plainly set down in the Scripture, and the best truths are the plainest of all. So, if anyone steps forward to be such a venerable *instructor of the world* that no man may appear to have said anything like him in his own age or in generations past, I am truly blunt enough to boldly pronounce that I suspect that person is significantly influenced by spiritual *pride and melancholy* <note>In the 17th century, "melancholy" was often associated with religious delusions or "enthusiasm."</note>. For, thank God, the *Gospel* is such a plain rule of *life* and *belief* for the sincere and obedient soul that no man can add anything to it.

But then, for a comparison of persons: what foolishness is it for any man—just because he can read the *common alphabet of honesty* and a *pious life* in the history of the Old and New Testament, finely allegorizing (as he imagines) those external *events* <note>original: "Transactions"; the historical deeds and occurrences recorded in the Bible.</note> into a *mysterious application* of what concerns...

...concerns the *internal self* <note>original: "inward man"</note>. It is a very unreasonable and rash thing—if not impious and blasphemous—for any person to place themselves, or for others to place them, on the same level as *Jesus Christ the Son of God*. He is the *Savior of men* and the *Prince of the highest orders of angels* <note>original: "Angelical Orders"</note>. He rose from the grave by the omnipotent hand of his Father and was seen to ascend into heaven by his Apostles, who gazed upon him as he passed through the clouds. All true Christians expect him to visibly appear there again and revisit the world according to his promise. I say, it seems to me quite wrong to acknowledge any man whatsoever as comparable to such a *sacred Person* as he proved himself to be in every way, and who was approved by a voice from heaven, saying, *This is my beloved Son, hear him.*

Therefore, if any person lacks these testimonies from heaven and cannot perform any miracles beyond what other men can do, yet is so arrogant <note>original: "unmannerly"</note> as to place themselves in the same rank as *Christ the Son of God*—simply because they have some "fine fancies" and phrases, and special interpretations of Scripture which they claim are immediately suggested by the *Spirit*—I cannot refrain from stating again that this person is overtaken with a high degree of either *Pride* or *Madness*. If they can persuade any others to look upon them as such a sacred Prophet, it must be due to *inattention* <note>original: "Inadvertency"</note> or *ignorance* on the followers' part. Indeed, I think I am not wrong to attribute their mistake to a kind of *Pride* as well. For *Pride* values nothing more than *Singularity* <note>The desire to be unique, elite, or set apart from the common crowd.</note>. Therefore, by undervaluing the plain simplicity of ordinary Christianity, such as is clearly presented in the *Gospel* of *Christ*, they think it is a great privilege to have a Prophet of their own. Specifically, they gain the advantage of being able to immediately judge—as they imagine—the truth or falsehood of everyone who ventures to speak outside the path of their own *Sect*, as if everyone were bound to learn their lessons from the sect's own book. It is a fine thing to become so "accurately wise" at such a cheap rate, and to "discover" who is *Spiritual*, and who is the *Carnal* or merely *Moral man*. This is indeed the folly of all *Sects*. I know of no better way to be freed from such enticements <note>original: "inveiglements"</note> than by earnestly striving after that which they all pretend to have: to become truly more holy

It shall at length come to pass that justice, peace, and equity shall flourish more universally and fully in the world than they ever yet have done; that faith in God and in the life to come shall be more vigorously sealed upon the hearts of men; and that there shall be a nearer union and conjunction between the human and divine nature in us than ever before, with more frequent and perceptible <note>original: "sensible"</note> commerce between the inhabitants of the *Heavenly* <note>original: "Aethereal"</note> and *Earthly* <note>original: "Terresterial"</note> regions, just as I have already declared concerning the *Seventh day* <note>The "Seventh Day" refers to the Sabbath of the world, a predicted millennium of peace and spiritual perfection.</note> in this *Defense of the Moral Cabbala*.

<meta>This page continues Henry More's argument regarding the interpretation of apocalyptic prophecy. He is transitioning from a discussion of the spiritual nature of Christ's kingdom to explaining why the "destruction" prophesied in the Bible should be understood spiritually rather than as physical violence.</meta>

# The Defence of the Moral Cabbala. CHAP. III.

<margin>
Revelation, Chapters 17 and 18.
2 Corinthians 10:4.
</margin>
This destruction should not necessarily be understood as physical <note>original: "carnal"</note> warfare or the shedding of blood, but as that warfare which *is not physical*, as *St. Paul* says. Similarly, the "Reign of the Saints" will not come about by invading the rights of Princes under the pretense that they lack "Saintship," but by the conversion of both Prince and people everywhere into the condition of Saints. The burning of *Rome* by fire is no more intended by that tragic prediction in the Apocalypse than the sacking of *Corinth* was intended by *St. Paul's* "weapons of warfare," which he boasts are so mighty through God for pulling down strongholds.

*Furthermore, I will add* that it is not only unnecessary to understand these predictions in such a literal <note>original: "gross"</note> way, but there is far greater reason to conclude that they are not meant that way at all. This is clear whether we consider the events predicted or the phrases and symbolic figures <note>original: "prefigurations"</note> used in the prophecies. It would contribute greatly to the peace and happiness of *Christendom* if some capable writer were employed to specifically explain such an important *truth*. 

Besides gratifying those noble-minded <note>original: "ingenuous"</note> people whose understandings cannot rest easily with any theory that clashes with the demonstrable order of visions—both simultaneous <note>original: "Synchronal"</note> and successive—which *Mr. Mede* <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638) was an influential English scholar whose "Key to the Revelation" established a systematic way of interpreting biblical prophecy.</note> has so happily discovered. Outside of his methods, all interpretations are found to be groundless and unsuitable, strained and confused. Nor can people's hearts be at ease if those threats and encouragements to revenge, wars, and bloodshed were the real goal and meaning of these *Apocalyptic* visions, rather than being understood figuratively and spiritually—which is undoubtedly their chief and primary, if not only, sense. Once this theory is accepted, it would prevent all the misuse that might be made of these clear and wonderful predictions; it would also remove any cause for prejudice or disgust against the most rational and consistent interpretations of them.

However, out of my love for the peace and tranquility of the Church—and not to lull her into a false sense of security—it does not follow that just because this storm of destruction is not literally meant for her, she will never suffer such a fate. For certainly, there could be such a state of affairs that, if the Church were to fall into it, would surely bring down divine vengeance even if God had never threatened it. 

For example: suppose the majority of the leaders of Christendom were gross idolaters, or bold nullifiers <note>original: "Nullers"</note> and abolishers of the essential laws of Christ through their own corrupt institutions. Suppose they were bloody and barbarous persecutors and murderers of those who, out of conscience toward God, will not commit idolatry with them nor forsake Christ’s commands. Suppose that to arm and harden themselves in this devilish falling away <note>original: "Apostasy"</note>, they should secretly harbor in their own hearts—and try to pass on to others—that hideous monster of *Atheism* and *Unbelief*. Imagine they took it as their fundamental principle that "all things are equally true in religion," and believed they must only have the wit to dictate whatever most increases the power and profit of the priest, making his self-interest the measure of everything, rather than the honor of God or the salvation of the people. 

I say, if they should collapse into such a dreadful apostasy as this, it is unimaginable how vengeance could be kept from overtaking them in the long run, or what hope they could have to fare any better 

<meta>The text continues on the next page with a comparison of the Church's fate to that of other fallen systems.</meta>

<summary>Henry More argues that apocalyptic prophecies of destruction should be interpreted as spiritual transformations rather than literal physical warfare. He warns, however, that the Church remains vulnerable to divine judgment if its leaders fall into idolatry, corruption, and atheism.</summary>

# CHAP. III. The Defence of the Moral Cabbala.

<margin>Matthew 23:38.</margin>
...then the Jews—those murderers of the prophets of old—of whom *Christ* declares that for persecuting and killing his innocent servants, all the righteous blood shed upon Earth should come upon them, from the blood of righteous *Abel* to the blood of *Zacharias* the son of *Barachias*, whom they slew between the Temple and the Altar. And what a sad vengeance it was that did at last overtake them, though they were the unique <note>original: "peculiar"</note> people of God, is well enough known—unless it were better considered.

<margin>
Job 21.
Amos 2.
Isaiah 30.
</margin>
If any such thing should ever come to pass—which God forbid <note>original: "avert"</note>—the very external surface <note>original: "Cortex"</note> of the prophetic visions would then incidentally <note>original: "ex accidenti"</note> seem prophetic. The arrangement <note>original: "contexture"</note> of phrases and symbolic figures <note>original: "prefigurations"</note> would be such as if they were intended to be a sort of Delphic sword <note>original: "δελφικὴ μάχαιρα"; a tool that serves two purposes at once</note>—a *two-edged sword* striking both ways. It would thus destroy in a literal <note>original: "gross"</note> sense those who had hardened themselves against the spiritual edge of the word, and who would not allow their foul abominations to be cut off, nor that bloody and idolatrous beastliness, which had ruled so long, to be slain by it. To as many as such a modest sense as this seems intolerable, they cannot but seem to me either atheistically foolish <note>original: "sottiſh"</note> and utterly unbelieving of any truth in either prophecies or Providence—thinking that human wit and force will carry all before it—or else they are in a sleepy, self-condemned condition, and hate the light because their deeds are evil. They are such as *say unto God, "Depart from us, we do not desire the knowledge of your ways"*; or such as *give the Nazarites wine to drink and command the prophets, saying, "Do not prophesy"*; who *say to the seers, "Do not see," and to the prophets, "Do not prophesy right things to us; speak smooth things to us, prophesy deceits."*

<margin>Daniel 7:27.</margin>
But unless I myself were to be a false and deceitful interpreter of the prophets, I cannot but profess my belief that the more excellent <note>original: "Eximious"</note> and illustrious Kingdom of *Christ* on Earth is yet to come. It will, in due time, be accomplished one way or another, according to what *Daniel* predicted: *That the kingdom, and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.* This has not yet happened, because that *little horn* which speaks such great things is not yet silenced.

<margin>Daniel 7:6.</margin>
This *little horn* cannot be *Antiochus Epiphanes*, as he plainly belongs to the *Leopard with four heads* or to the *Goat with four horns*. These beasts denote the *Greek Kingdom*, of which the *great horn*, or *Alexander the Great*, is accounted the first king, and the other *four* as his successors (otherwise, how could he be *first*?). *Antiochus* is reckoned to be in the later time of the kingdom of the *four horns*. This further shows that the successors of *Alexander's* successors all belong to that one kingdom styled "Greek," represented by the entire bodies of those beasts: the *Leopard* (with four heads and four wings) and the *He-goat* (with four horns after the breaking of that first great one). From this, it is necessary that the *fourth beast* be the *Roman Empire*, which has also been the constant opinion of the Church and the Church Fathers.

<margin>Revelation 11:15.</margin>
At these same times and events, *St. John* points to the same thing as *Daniel* at the blast of the seventh trumpet: *And the seventh angel sounded, and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of the world are*

<summary>Henry More argues that the "Kingdom of Christ" is a future reality and identifies the "fourth beast" of Daniel's prophecy as the Roman Empire rather than the Greek kingdom of Antiochus. He warns that those who reject the spiritual meaning of prophecy risk a literal, destructive judgment like that which befell the ancient Jews.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Henry More’s discussion of the eventual triumph of Christ’s kingdom. # The Defence of the Moral Cabbala. CHAP. III.

*...become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ, and he shall reign for ever and ever.*

<margin>
1 Corinthians 15:24, 25, 26.
* Daniel 7:14, 27.
</margin>
And lastly, the Apostle Paul also witnesses that *before Christ delivers up the kingdom to his Father, he is to put down all rule, and all authority and power; for he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.* As I have already explained to you, although death is now the "King of Terrors," in that great festival and Sabbath-rest <note>original: "Sabbatisme"; referring to a period of spiritual peace or the Millennium</note>, because of such a sensible and palpable union between the heavenly and earthly natures, it will be but a pleasant passage into a higher room. Or, to use that more mysterious expression of the Rabbis concerning Moses—in whose writings this Sabbath-rest is foreshadowed <note>original: "adumbrated"</note>—God will draw a man’s soul up to himself by an "amorous kiss."

<margin>
Rabbi Maimonides, *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: *More Nevochim*</note>, part 3, chapter 51.
</margin>
For such was the death of that holy man Moses, who is said to have died in Moab "at the mouth of the Lord" <note>original: על פי יהוה (*al pi YHWH*); traditionally interpreted by the Rabbis as "by a kiss of the Lord"</note>, in the kisses and embraces of God.

This shall be the condition of the Church of Christ for many hundreds of years, until the wheel of Providence drives further on and the stage of history <note>original: "things"</note> draws toward its final period; then, men shall not only be freed from the fear and pain of death, but there shall be no possibility of dying at all.

<margin>
2 Peter 3:10.
</margin>
*For then shall the day of the Lord come, in which the heavens shall pass away with a noise, and the elements melt with fervent heat, and the earth with all the things in it shall be burned up.* Thus, once Christ has taken vengeance upon the obstinately wicked and disobedient and has fully triumphed over all his enemies, he will give up his kingdom to his Father, whose deputy <note>original: "Vicegerent"</note> he has been until now in the affairs of both men and angels. But until then, whoever—by pretending to be more spiritual and mystical than other men—would smother those essential principles of the Christian religion that refer to the *historical person* <note>original: "external Person"</note> of Christ, let him phrase it as well as he likes or speak as magnificently of himself as he can, we must never let go of the plain and justifiable faith of the Word for ungrounded fancies and fine sayings.

Therefore, let every person seek God individually and search out the truth in the Holy Scripture, preparing themselves for a right understanding of it by steadfastly and sincerely practicing those things that are plainly and undeniably contained within it. Let them expect illumination according to the best way it is communicated—that is, in a way that corresponds to our own human faculties. Otherwise, if we say goodbye to all reason, history, and human assistance and learning <note>original: "Acquisitions"</note>, the world will never be rid of religious delusions <note>original: "Lunacies"</note> and fantasies.

<summary>More describes the final victory of Christ over death, using the Rabbinic concept of "death by a kiss" to illustrate a peaceful transition to the afterlife during the Millennium. He warns against "extreme spiritualists" who deny the historical Christ and argues that faith must be balanced with reason and Scripture to avoid religious delusion.</summary>

# The Moral Cabbala.

### CHAPTER I.

1. **MAN** is a **Microcosm** <term>A "little world" or miniature representation of the entire universe</term> or "Little World," in whom there are two principles: Spirit and Flesh. 2. *The earthly or fleshly nature appears first.* 4. *The light of conscience is not looked up to.* 6. *The spirit of insightful and affectionate discernment between good and evil.* 10. *The excessive desires of the flesh are driven aside and limited.* 11. *As a result, the plants of righteousness bear fruit and flourish.* 16. *The hearty and sincere love of God and one's neighbor is like the Sun in the human soul; purely intellectual theories <note>original: "Notionality"</note> and opinions are like the weak and faint light of the scattered stars.* 18. *Those who walk in sincere love walk in the Day; those who are guided by mere intellectual theory travel in the Night.* 22. *The natural desiring faculty <term>original: "Concupiscible"; the part of the soul driven by physical desire</term> brings forth by the command of God and is corrected by devotion.* 24. *The spirited faculty <term>original: "Irascible"; the part of the soul driven by anger or passion</term> also brings forth.* 26. *Christ, the image of God, is created, being a perfect ruler over all the movements of the spirited and desiring faculties.* 29. *The food of the Divine Life.* 30. *The food of the Animal Life.* 31. *The Divine Wisdom approves of whatever is simply natural as being good.*

# The Defense of the Threefold Cabbala.

## The INTRODUCTION.

1. **Diodorus's** mistake concerning **Moses**, and other lawgivers who have claimed to have received their laws from either God or some good angel. 2. Reasons why **Moses** began his history with the creation of the world. 3. The Sun and Moon identified as the Egyptians' **Osiris** and **Isis**, and how they came to be worshipped as gods. 4. The **deification** <note>original: "Apotheosis"</note>

of mortal men, such as **Bacchus** and **Ceres**, and how this practice first entered the world. 5. That the literal text of the Scripture typically speaks of physical <note>original: "Philosophical"</note> things according to the perception and imagination of the common people <term>original: "the Vulgar"</term>. 6. That there is a deeper physical meaning hidden within the literal text of the first three chapters of **Genesis**. 7. That there is a moral or mystical sense not only in these three chapters, but in several other places of the Scripture.

# The Defense of the Literal Cabbala.

## CHAPTER I.

1. The genuine sense of "In the Beginning." The differences between the Hebrew words *bara* <note>meaning: "to create"</note>, *asah* <note>meaning: "to make"</note>, and *kanah* <note>meaning: "to possess or acquire"</note> were neglected by the **Seventy** <term>The "Seventy" refers to the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</term>, who translated *bara* only as "he made" <note>original Greek: ἐποίησεν</note>. 2. The reason for their mistake discovered, namely those who believe **Moses** implies that matter is uncreated. That "the Spirit of God" <note>original Hebrew: *Ruach Elohim* (רוח אלהים)</note> is no more than "a great wind" <note>original Latin: *ventus magnus*</note>. 4, 5. That the first darkness was not properly "Night." 6. Why the **Seventy** translate *raquia* <note>the Hebrew word for the expanse of the sky</note> as "Firmament" <note>original Latin: *Firmamentum*</note>, and that it is in allusion to a firmly pitched tent. 11. That the visible effects of the Sun invited the Pagans to idolatry, and that their oracles taught them to call him by the name of **Iao** <note>A name for God used in ancient mystical and magical texts</note>. 14. That the Prophet **Jeremiah** <note>original: "Jeremy"</note> distinguishes the day from the **Sun**, speaking according to the understanding of the common people. 15. The reason why the stars appear on this side of the upper cerulean <note>sky-blue</note> sea. 27. The opinion of the **Anthropomorphites** <term>People who believe God has a physical human body</term>, and the great significance of common people imagining God in the shape of a man. **Aristophanes's** story in **Plato** regarding men and women growing together at first, as if they both made up only one animal.
->p. 57<-

## CHAPTER II.

7. The origin of the word "soul" <note>original Greek: ψυχὴ (*psuche*)</note> corresponds to the breathing of **Adam's** soul into 

<column-break/>

his nostrils. 8. The exact location of **Paradise**. That the **Gihon** river is part of the **Euphrates**; the **Pison** is either the **Phasis** or the **Phasitigris**. That the Metaphysical Hyle <term>prime matter</term> in the first day’s creation is not called "Earth" merely symbolically—a thing not hard to prove, but unnecessary. 129

### CHAPTER VIII.
1. That *Hyle* <term>the Greek term for "matter," specifically the raw, unformed substance from which the universe was created</term> or first Matter, is mere *Possibility* of being, according to *Aristotle*. 2. That the same is but *Empty Space* or *Capacity of Body*, according to *Plato* and *Plotinus*; and how aptly their description of *Hyle* agrees with Moses's "Earth without form and void" <note>original Latin: *Terra inanis & vacua*</note>. 3. Why *Moses* would take notice of so flimsy and vanishing <note>original: "evanid"</note> a matter as this *Hyle* seems to be in his *Six Days of Creation*. 8.
